Hi Olga —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Our architects asked for a short write-up comparing three ingress options for the private deployment: VPC peering, PrivateLink (or cloud provider interface endpoints), and a site-to-site VPN. Key constraints:
- No incoming public IPs for inference nodes (regulatory)
- Minimum MTU preservation for model payloads (~9000 preferred)
- Short-term: pilot in us-west-2; long-term: multi-region

Can you send a concise recommendation (network tradeoffs, failover story, cost order-of-magnitude, and any blockers for our procurement/security team)? Cara will own procurement questions.

Tim / Cara —

Attached is a short playbook and a cost sketch (see attached spreadsheet). High level:

1) VPC peering
- Pros: low latency, straightforward routing, full L3 access.
- Cons: cross-account limitations (per-region peering), no native private service abstraction, potential route table scale pain with many customers.
- Failure model: dependent on cloud backbone; single-region peering is typically resilient; cross-region requires additional peering or transit.
- When to pick: tight latency SLOs, customer controls entire VPC addressing and routing.

2) PrivateLink / Interface Endpoints
- Pros: service-oriented (L3/L4 optional), controlled surface area (only service ports), simpler for customers who want minimal routing changes. Supports endpoint policies.
- Cons: slightly higher egress cost for data processing + per-endpoint hourly charges; throughput per endpoint has limits (can be mitigated with multiple endpoints).
- Failure model: endpoint availability + AZ resilience; fallback can be to another endpoint or to a VPN path.
- When to pick: customers who cannot allow routing/peering changes, or require least-exposed surface.

3) Site-to-site VPN (S2S)
- Pros: quick to provision, works with on-prem and cloud CPE, supports encryption boundaries customers want.
- Cons: higher latency, asymptotic throughput depending on CPE, more ops overhead, MTU/fragmentation risks for jumbo frames.
- Failure model: depends on customer gateway; can be multi-tunnel for HA but adds complexity.
- When to pick: air-gapped or on-prem constrained environments where peering/endpoint options are blocked.

Recommendation (short): For Acrosoft pilot in us-west-2, recommend PrivateLink as primary with an S2S VPN as a documented fallback for regions/customers or where jumbo MTU is unsupported by endpoint networking. Reserve VPC peering for customers that require L3 access and are comfortable with cross-account routing.

Action items:
- Ben: provide a draft of endpoint scaling guidance and expected per-endpoint capacity limits (cc).
- Kimberly: validate procurement/legal on endpoint contract language + data egress cost model.
- Karthik: confirm MTU path preservation around endpoints and recommended TCP MSS clamp settings.

Quick note on throughput:
- Each PrivateLink interface endpoint (provider side) gives ~5-10 Gbps practical throughput depending on instance sizing; we recommend deploying multiple endpoints per AZ for production >5 Gbps.
- For peering, throughput is effectively limited by the customer's VPC link and our NICs — lower per-connection overhead vs. PL but requires route management.
- VPN numbers: expect variable throughput; many customers hit 1-2 Gbps limits depending on device.

I'll attach a short table in the spreadsheet with numbers and suggested instance sizes.

-ben

Cara —
We can provide SOC 2 Type II summary and a short attestation that PrivateLink traffic stays on the cloud provider backbone when endpoints are used. I'll draft a line for the SOW that calls out endpoint availability and the fallback pattern (PrivateLink primary; S2S for region-edge/MTU exceptions; peering only if customer requests L3).

Cost sketch (high level estimates, US-west-2, pilot):
- PrivateLink endpoints (4 endpoints, 2 AZs): $600–$900/month in endpoint-hour fees + data processing/GB at provider rates (~$0.02–$0.03/GB) -> ~ $200–$300 for 10 TB data processing + provider egress where applicable.
- S2S VPN: minimal hourly device costs but expect managed appliance / termination costs if we operate endpoints (~$300–$800/mo depending on throughput SLA).
- Peering: relatively cheap (no endpoint fee) but depends on customer cross-account data transfer pricing; typically similar to intra-region data transfer rates.

I'll attach the redlined SOW draft by EOD; Olga & Ben, flag anything you'd rather not commit to in the SOW.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
